**How one file works as both languages:**
- **The opening line `/* /* */`:** Rust lets comments sit inside other comments, but C++ doesn't. In C++ the first `*/` ends the comment, so the C++ code after it gets compiled. In Rust the comment is still open, so Rust ignores the C++ code.
- **`R"( */`:** C++ reads `R"(` as the start of a raw string that can span many lines, so the Rust code below it is just text to C++. Rust is still inside the comment, so it ignores `R"(` and reads ` */` as the end of the comment. The Rust code after that gets compiled.
- **The last line `/* )"; // */`:** C++ closes the raw string at `)"`, ends the statement with `;`, and ignores the rest after `//`. Rust sees the whole line as one comment.

Both versions add numbers digit by digit as decimal strings, so large N doesn't overflow. A plain 64-bit integer would overflow above N=91.
